messages:
incident-bot: :warning: Autoscaler error spike: provider rate-limit responses detected for cluster gpu-west-1. queue_depth=1350, scale_attempts=0, throttling=true

morgan: dashboards confirm sudden jump ~2.5m ago, lots of 429s coming from cloud provider API. customers seeing 5xx/429 on request tails.

zara: grabbing controller logs now. can someone page infra-oncall?

ben: autoscaler-controller logs: `ProviderAPIError: 429 Too Many Requests` then `entering backoff window for 300s`. stacktrace attached in logs.

infra-oncall: acknowledging. checking provider quota and active API usage. also verifying node pool max (current max_nodes=60).

support-ops: receiving tickets about degraded throughput from team-integ, media-svc, and retail-app. I'll draft an update.

morgan: priority mitigations: 1) divert non-critical traffic to fallback smaller model 2) enable per-tenant soft-rate-limits at edge 3) attach temporary preemptible capacity if possible

zara: implementing fallback routing for "best_effort" lanes: `routerctl set-route --lane best_effort --target fallback-xsmall`

deploy-bot: Route update started for fallback-xsmall (canary)

ben: manual scale attempt to attach nodes hits provider limit: `cloudctl resize --group rwd-gpu-west --size 80` returns 429 with Retry-After: 45s. autoscaler is still paused.

infra-oncall: opened a provider support case SR-77829, flagged urgent. Provider acknowledges throttling due to control-plane flood.

morgan: can we soft-throttle large tenants at the edge to reduce queue pressure? risk is customer experience for heavy users.

support-ops: applying soft-throttle profiles to media-svc and retail-app now. will roll canary at 5% then 50%.

zara: meanwhile, Ben — any chance to attach preemptible/burst pool via a different API path that isn't rate-limited?

ben: provider offered preemptible attach as a separate call; trying `cloudctl attach-preemptibles --count 10`. if it succeeds we'll have capacity in 3-7 mins, but slower GPUs.

deploy-bot: Attach job initiated for preemptible-pool (10 nodes)

infra-oncall: preemptibles are up (10 nodes) but they're A10-class; expect 20-30% higher latency on those jobs.

morgan: good — updating routing: best_effort -> preemptible-pool, high_priority unchanged.

zara: after routing and throttles, queue dropped from 1350 -> 480 over ~7 minutes. some error reduction observed.

sre-lead: note: autoscaler pausing entirely on provider 429 is dangerous. we need a policy to allow limited manual override during provider backoff. filing SRE ticket.

ben: logs show autoscaler resumed after backoff window; started adding nodes but limited by configured max_nodes. we should consider temporary bump to max_nodes during incidents.

infra-oncall: increased max_nodes from 60 -> 90 in cluster config; change committed with clear revert step and tagged with incident reference.

support-ops: customer-facing note queued: "We are seeing temporary degraded performance in gpu-west-1 due to cloud provider API throttling. We have applied mitigations (fallbacks and traffic shaping). We'll provide an update in 60 minutes."

morgan: post-mitigation: queue ~420, priority lane latency within SLO, best_effort still degraded but served by preemptibles. marking incident severity reduced to medium.

zara: collecting all relevant logs and `kubectl` outputs to attach to SR-77829 and internal tickets.

sre-lead: action items assigned: 1) autoscaler behavior on provider 429 -> change to 'soft-pause' and allow manual override (SRE-620) 2) add provider-rate-limit monitoring and alerting (OBS-412) 3) runbook for attaching preemptible pool and routing fallback (INFRA-777) 4) customer comms template for capacity events (CS-210)

ben: I'll upload autoscaler logs + commands used to the incident ticket.

morgan: going to keep channel open for 45m monitoring window. If stable, convert to a postmortem draft tomorrow with a detailed timeline.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation=in-progress->stabilized, monitor_window=45m, impacted_customers=team-integ, media-svc, retail-app, severity=medium

support-ops: posted customer message. will ping if any new spikes.

infra-oncall: provider requested our mitigation steps; they've temporarily raised API limits and continue investigation into control-plane throttling.

zara: final check at last_message_ts=1992504675: queue=410, autoscaler healthy, preemptible_nodes_in_use=6/10.

morgan: thanks for quick work. we'll track follow-ups in SRE-620, OBS-412, INFRA-777, CS-210. closing live mitigation stage — keeping channel open for monitoring. :white_check_mark:
